content.value_statement: Teams need consistent Drizzle ORM patterns for PostgreSQL projects. This skill provides schema, relation, query, mutation, transaction, and migration examples.
actual_capabilities: Shows Drizzle pgTable schema definitions with inferred select and insert types.
Demonstrates one-to-many relation definitions between users and posts.
Provides query examples for filters, sorting, relation loading, and limits.
Shows insert, update, delete, and transaction patterns.
Lists Drizzle Kit generate, push, and studio commands.
Includes a Drizzle config pattern for PostgreSQL credentials.
limitations: Focuses on PostgreSQL and node-postgres; other database dialects are not covered.
Does not include a full migration folder structure.
Does not cover validation, authorization, or API layer integration.
Requires users to adapt table names, types, and credentials.

use_cases.title: Scaffold a Database Layer
use_cases.description: Create consistent schema, relation, and client patterns for a new TypeScript application.

use_cases.title: Review Query Style
use_cases.description: Compare project queries against simple Drizzle patterns for filters, sorting, and relation loading.

use_cases.title: Standardize Migrations
use_cases.description: Document common Drizzle Kit commands for generating, applying, and inspecting database migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use drizzle-patterns to outline a PostgreSQL user schema with inferred types. Explain each field choice in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Add Relations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use drizzle-patterns to design relations between users and posts. Include the purpose of each relation and reference field.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use drizzle-patterns to review these Drizzle queries for filtering, sorting, relation loading, and return shape consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Migration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use drizzle-patterns to plan a safe migration workflow for a new table. Include generation, review, application, and rollback considerations.

output_examples.input: Create a Drizzle user schema for a PostgreSQL app.
output_examples.output: A users table plan with UUID primary keys, unique email, profile fields, timestamps, and inferred TypeScript model guidance.

output_examples.input: Show how to query verified users with posts.
output_examples.output: A query approach using relation loading, a verified-email filter, newest-first sorting, and a small result limit.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration for a new profiles table.
output: Define the profiles table and relation.
Generate a migration with Drizzle Kit.
Review database changes before applying them.

best_practices: Keep credentials in environment variables and never hardcode database URLs.
Review generated migrations before applying them to shared databases.
Reuse inferred insert and select types across service code.
anti_patterns: Do not run schema push against production without review.
Do not paste real connection strings into prompts, examples, or commits.
Do not copy sample table names without matching business requirements.

faq.question: What database does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets PostgreSQL projects that use Drizzle ORM with TypeScript.

faq.question: Does it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides database patterns that users adapt inside their own application structure.

faq.question: Can Claude or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it store database credentials?
faq.answer: No. It shows environment variable references and does not include real credential values.

faq.question: Does it cover migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common Drizzle Kit commands for generation, push, and Studio usage.

faq.question: What should users customize first?
faq.answer: Users should customize table names, field types, relations, and migration process details.
